alt: The Scenic Sorcerer editor showing a demo inn called The Gilded Stag: a wooden common room with a long table, chairs, a fireplace and a bar, a stone kitchen, a round purple wizard's tower with a spiral staircase, a rocky cellar with a staircase down, chests and a glowing blue circle, a triangular orchard and a grassy yard with a well and a tent. Red numbered markers, a warning triangle and sun-like light icons are on top. Tools run down the left and settings down the right.
caption: The editor with a demo map. Tools on the left, settings on the right. The red numbers, the triangle and the sun-like icons are GM notes and lights, which only the GM sees. The furniture and props are stamps.

alt: The Stamp tool open on the same map. The right-hand panel shows a search box, a list of stamp kinds set to Tavern and kitchen, and a grid of small pictures of baths, campfires, a chopping board, goblets and iron pots, with a credit line for Tom Cartos underneath.
caption: 676 painted props come with it, in 14 kinds, from furniture to farm gear, and you can add pictures of your own. They are by Tom Cartos, used under his Open Map License, and he is credited in the panel.

alt: A sampler map of seventeen staircases on a stone floor: twelve straight ones in stone, wood, metal, rock, moss, ice, snow and dirt, and five round spiral ones along the bottom. Each has shaded steps that grow lighter toward the high end, and most have an arrow. The first spiral is selected, and the panel on the right shows its steps, winding direction, material and arrow.
caption: The stairs are drawn by the editor in the floor materials, not from pictures. The steps shade as they climb, an arrow shows the way, and a selected staircase can change its number of steps, material and direction, or wind the other way.

alt: A sampler of fourteen square rooms, each with a different painted floor and its name on it: stone, wood, dirt, grass, water, snow, ice, mossy, rocky, forest, magical, lava, metal and plain.
caption: Thirteen floor textures and a plain colour, all painted by code, so they stay sharp at any size. A brush can paint them freehand too.

alt: The inn map with the long dining table selected and a right-click menu open beside it, offering Bring to front, Move up a layer, Move down a layer, Send to back, Copy, Duplicate, Flip and Delete.
caption: Right-click a thing for its menu: move it up or down a layer, copy, duplicate, flip or delete. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Alt+drag to drag a copy, and a list of keyboard shortcuts work too.

alt: The inn map with the triangular orchard selected: small round dots sit on its three corners, eight small squares sit on a dashed box round it, and the panel on the right lists the floor choices and explains what the dots and squares do.
caption: Select a room and it grows handles. The round dots on the corners reshape it, so a triangle can go obtuse or acute. The squares on the box round it stretch it, and Shift keeps its proportions.

alt: The inn map with the lighting preview on: the map is dim, the common room is warm from the fireplace, the tower glows violet, and a pool of light surrounds the campfire in the yard.
caption: Lighting preview. The map goes dark except where lights reach, walls stop the light, and a window lets a little out. The same lights go into the exports.

alt: The editor on an Upper floor level: a wooden gallery joined by a bridge to a round turret, with the ground floor's rooms showing faintly underneath. The Levels list on the right shows Upper floor and Ground floor.
caption: Several levels in one map. The level below shows faintly, so a room upstairs can be lined up with the rooms under it.

alt: A hex-grid map called The Ashen Marches: a blue lake, a grey hill range, a small walled fort, a brown road and patches of grass, over a pointy-topped hex grid, with labels for Lake Vael, the Ashen Hills and Fort Kerrin.
caption: A hex map. The grid can be flat-top or pointy-top, and a picture of it is sized from the cell so the hexes line up in the tabletop.

alt: The Export dialog over the editor: pixels per cell, a size readout, picture options for grid lines, GM notes and baked lighting, a file type choice, and buttons for a picture, a Universal VTT file and a Foundry scene.
caption: The Export dialog. One picture, or files for a virtual tabletop that carry the walls, doors, windows and lights with them.

alt: A clean picture of the inn map exported at 1680 by 1120 pixels, with its furniture, stairs and floors, and with no grid lines, no room numbers and no light icons.
caption: What a tabletop receives: a clean picture, with no grid lines and no GM notes, because the tabletop draws its own grid and keeps the walls separately.
